# C22: Late swap v2: live-score conditioning

**State:** Optimizer. **Size:** M (one session, about 1 to 2 hours, three checkpoints). **Depends on:** C10, C13. **Parallel with:** none (every chunk touches `cli.py`, `CONTRACTS.md` and settings; run one at a time).

**Changelog:** 2026-10-14 (ADJUDICATION-R2 entry R2-34, final audit): under the data posture `nba_api` is never used for live data; finished games use box scores after the final; with no permitted live stat source, the partial-game path is off and labeled for in-progress games unless the owner approves a source through a change request (the path is still built and tested on fixtures), consistent with R2-19. 2026-10-14 (ADJUDICATION-R2): `LiveState` carries, per in-progress game and player, cumulative box-score stats (`pts, fg3m, reb, ast, stl, blk, tov`) and minutes played; `simulate_game_partial` simulates the remaining stats conditional on that state, adds them to the cumulative stats and applies `score_line` once to the completed line, never adding two separately bonus-scored fantasy totals; a game with only fantasy points so far loses the partial-game path with a labeled fallback, while finished games can still use exact final fantasy points; new tests for a double-double crossed during the remainder, one already earned before the snapshot, and a triple-double transition, each also at Captain (R2-19); the swap keeps the time-to-lock label (CONTRACTS 11.7 "Time to lock", R2-6) and the download freshness refusal (R2-14); usage budget added. 2026-10-14: created.

## Goal, and why it sits here

Make the post-lock swap see the scoreboard. C10's swap re-optimizes open slots with locked games still at their pre-lock distributions, so at 9:30 pm it pretends the 7:00 pm games have not happened. This chunk conditions each scenario on what is known: finished games take their actual DraftKings points (from box scores published after the final, under the D1 posture, otherwise from a standings file the owner downloads mid-slate). In-progress games need box-score stats and minutes so far; under the data posture `nba_api` is never used for live data and no permitted live stat source exists, so the partial-game path is off and labeled unless the owner approves a source through a change request. With an approved source, an in-progress game takes each player's box-score stats and minutes so far, simulates the rest of the game as stats with the variance scaled by the share of the game left, adds them, and scores the completed line once so the double-double and triple-double bonuses come out right; this chunk builds and tests that path on fixtures so it is ready. A mid-slate standings file carries only fantasy points, so it can settle a finished game but not an in-progress one; such a game keeps its pre-lock distribution and the brief says so. The scope rule from C10 stays: only entries whose news state changed or whose improvement clears the threshold are rewritten. It needs C13's standings parser. B-D-02, conditioning on the opponents' locked lineups from a mid-slate standings export, stays in the backlog with its trigger.

## Scope

**Build:**

- `resolve/live.py`: `live_state(slate, now, sources, settings) -> LiveState`: per game, `status` in finished, in progress, not started. Finished games: each player's final box-score line from the box-score adapter after the final (C05's history source, under the D1 posture), scored once with `score_line`, when present; else exact final DraftKings points from a mid-slate standings file parsed by C13's parser with `TimeRemaining` above 0 allowed only on this path and the result labeled `source = "standings_midslate"` (exact final fantasy points are enough to condition a finished game). In-progress games: under the D1 posture `nba_api` is never used for live data and no permitted live stat source exists, so by default every in-progress game has `partial_available = false`, keeps its pre-lock distribution (the C10 behavior), and the brief labels it ("<game>: in progress, no permitted live stat source; kept at its pre-lock distribution"). Only with a live stat source the owner has approved through a change request does an in-progress game take each player's cumulative box-score stats so far (`pts, fg3m, reb, ast, stl, blk, tov`) and minutes played from that source, and `fraction_remaining` from the game clock when the source carries it, else from `dfs live "<AWAY>@<HOME> <quarter> <mm:ss>"` typed by the owner. If only fantasy points so far are available for an in-progress game (for example only the standings file), or no clock is known, the partial-game path is unavailable for that game: `partial_available = false`, the game keeps its pre-lock distribution (the C10 behavior), and the brief labels the fallback ("<game>: in progress, only fantasy points so far; kept at its pre-lock distribution"). Not-started games untouched. Everything snapshotted.
- `sim/partial.py`: `simulate_game_partial(night, game_id, S, seed, stats_so_far, minutes_so_far, fraction_remaining)`: the C07 bottom-up draw for the rest of the game, conditional on the state: each player's remaining minutes equal projected minutes times `fraction_remaining`, with hard caps applied to `minutes_so_far` plus the remainder; stat rates unchanged; the variance of each remaining stat scaled by the same fraction. The simulated remaining stats are added to `stats_so_far`, and `score_line` (C04a, vectorized by C05) is applied once to each completed line, so the double-double and triple-double bonuses are judged on the full-game line and Captain is 1.5 times that bonus-inclusive total. It never adds two separately bonus-scored fantasy totals (points so far plus points for the remainder), which would miss a double-double crossed in the remainder or award one twice (ADJUDICATION-R2 R2-19). A finished game is the special case `fraction_remaining = 0` with zero variance: its final line scored once, or its exact final fantasy points when only those are available. Keyed draws leave other games' columns untouched; points are float32 exact eighth points (CONTRACTS section 7 precision rule).
- `swap --live` (C10's `swap` given a `LiveState`): build the conditioned scenario set for the slate, re-optimize open slots against it, keep the C10 scope rule (`news_state_hash` changed or improvement at least `swap.min_improvement_points`), the concentration re-check, the diff, the "valid until" stamp, the time-to-lock label (CONTRACTS 11.7 "Time to lock": only a locked cell or an unresolved lock time blocks a row; a row locking within `export.tight_minutes` is exported and labeled tight) and the freshness refusal (a download older than the latest started tip is refused, CONTRACTS 11.5). The brief's swap block names each game's status and source, and any game on the fallback.
- `dfs swap --slate <key> --live [--standings <file>]` and `dfs live "<game> <clock>"`.
- Late-swap scorecard rows (C13): per swap night, entries rewritten, predicted against realized improvement, and when the triggering news became available against when the owner could act; these rows are the trigger evidence for backlog item B-D-02.

**Out of scope:** B-D-02 (locked-field conditioning: opponents' locked lineups from the mid-slate export; backlog until the late-swap scorecard shows how often late scratches changed our entries); B-D-03 (game-script regimes for blowouts; backlog with its own trigger); any live-odds feed; the watcher (C17).

## Contracts

- **Consumes:** `swap`, `resolve`, the drill harness (C10); `simulate_game`, `ScenarioSet` (C07); the standings parser (C13); the box-score adapter and the vectorized `score_line` (C05, from C04a's function); `Ledger`, `validate`, `export` (C03); the freshness helper (C11a); `NewsState` (C06).
- **Produces:** `LiveState(slate_key, as_of, games: {game_id: {status, source, fraction_remaining, partial_available: bool, fallback_reason: str | None, stats_so_far: {person_key: {pts, fg3m, reb, ast, stl, blk, tov}}, minutes_so_far: {person_key: float}, final_points: {person_key: float}}})`: cumulative box-score stats and minutes played per player for in-progress games (and finished games when the box score has them), exact final fantasy points (float32 eighths) for finished games; `simulate_game_partial(night, game_id, S, seed, stats_so_far, minutes_so_far, fraction_remaining)`; `dfs swap --live`, `dfs live`, the late-swap scorecard rows. `LiveState` and the partial-game signature go into CONTRACTS.md sections 7 and 11.5 in the same commit.

## Definition of done

- Finished game: every scenario column for that game's players equals the actual points, variance zero; a player who did not play gets zero.
- In-progress game on a hand-made fixture: the mean of each remaining stat equals projected minutes times the fraction remaining times the per-minute rate, and each completed stat equals the stat so far plus the remainder; the variance of each remaining stat equals its full-game variance times the fraction; `fraction_remaining = 1` with zero stats and minutes so far reproduces the C07 draw exactly.
- Bonuses scored once on the completed line (R2-19), each case checked at UTIL and at Captain (1.5 times the bonus-inclusive total) against `score_line` applied to the completed line: (a) a double-double crossed during the remainder (8 points and 9 rebounds so far: scenarios whose remainder adds at least 2 points and 1 rebound earn the bonus once, the others none); (b) a double-double already earned before the snapshot (12 points and 11 rebounds so far: the bonus appears exactly once in every scenario, never twice); (c) a triple-double transition (12 points, 10 rebounds and 8 assists so far: scenarios whose remainder adds at least 2 assists carry the triple-double bonuses by C05's confirmed rule, with no bonus counted twice). A static test shows no code path adds two separately scored fantasy totals.
- Fantasy-points-only fallback: with only a mid-slate standings file, a finished game is conditioned on its exact final points (labeled `standings_midslate`), and an in-progress game has `partial_available = false`, columns byte-identical to its pre-lock draw, and the fallback named in the brief.
- Not-started games have byte-identical columns before and after conditioning.
- Source order: finished games from box scores after the final when present, else the mid-slate standings file (labeled); in-progress games keep the C10 behavior with the "no permitted live stat source" label unless an owner-approved live source exists, in which case they use its box-score stats and minutes, with the clock from the source, else the typed clock; an in-progress game with only fantasy points so far, or with no clock, keeps the C10 behavior with the fallback labeled; with no live source at all, the C10 behavior with the brief saying "no live scores".
- The mid-slate standings file is accepted only on this path; `dfs results` still refuses it.
- Swap on `fixtures/dk/2026-10-15/post_lock_entries.csv` with a conditioned set: locked cells byte-identical; only entries meeting the scope rule change; the diff lists every change; the file validates; a changed row locking within `export.tight_minutes` is exported and labeled tight; the run finishes inside `resolve.budget_s`. A download older than the latest started tip is refused with the plain message.
- Determinism: the same live state twice gives byte-identical files.
- The scorecard rows exist after a swap night.

## What I check

On a real evening with staggered tips, after the first games finish, download one standings file for the main Classic and run:

```bash
uv run dfs swap --slate classic_main --live --standings "<path to the download>"
```

Expected: a header like "2 games final (actual points from your download), 1 in progress (no permitted live stat source; kept at its pre-lock distribution), 9 not started" (only with a live source you approved through a change request would it read "1 in progress (box score with 14 minutes left)"); then a short diff of changed cells with every locked cell untouched, and a new versioned file that validates. Save that standings file hashed as `fixtures/standings/midslate_<date>.zip` for the tests. Next morning `dfs results` should show the late-swap rows.

## Size estimate and checkpoints

About 1 to 2 hours. Checkpoint 1: `LiveState` with the three sources, the stats and minutes so far, the mid-slate relaxation and the fantasy-points-only fallback (commit). Checkpoint 2: the partial-game draw on stats, scored once, with its tests including the three bonus cases (commit). Checkpoint 3: `swap --live`, the scorecard rows, the real-evening check (commit).

## Usage budget

About 25% of a five-hour window and 4% of a weekly window (estimates until measured). If the session passes 40% of a five-hour window, stop at the next checkpoint and hand off.

## Risks

- **No permitted live stat source.** Under D1, `nba_api` is for box scores and game logs of finished games and is never used for live data; finished games use box scores after the final or the owner's standings download, and in-progress games keep their pre-lock distribution with the fallback label (the partial-game path needs stats, not fantasy points) unless the owner approves a live source through a change request; the brief says which was used.
- **Box scores lag during the night.** The standings download is the fallback for finished games (its `FPTS` values are DraftKings' own numbers); an in-progress game without box-score stats keeps its pre-lock distribution and the brief says so, because fantasy points alone cannot place the bonuses correctly.
- **Blowouts break the linear remaining-minutes rule.** Known and accepted; B-D-03 in the backlog covers garbage-time regimes with its trigger.
- **Swap churn late in the night.** The scope rule and `swap.min_improvement_points` limit it; if more than 30% of entries change, the brief asks for confirmation as in C10.
